reader_start: The reader knows the classical equation, energy law, local theory, and Sobolev tools, but has not seen why a critical-height escalation should generate a two-index jet or why finite rectangles are the right terminal objects.
live_pressure: Each new formal object must arrive after its mathematical need has become visible, while every later use must remain downstream of its actual prerequisites.

move.selection: Retain every load-bearing equation and theorem while rebuilding the surrounding exposition around the proof spine and its explanatory branch.
move.connection: Let energy and VPI create the critical-height problem, let temporal escalation create the mixed jet, let height-spatial nesting create the need for compatible finite cuts, and let the rectangle theorem create the endpoint problem.
move.development: Give each difficult connection enough prose and local calculation for the reader to understand why the next object is necessary; compress standard background and repeated formal packaging.
move.expression: Use direct mathematical subjects and actions, varied sentence lengths, complete thoughts, stable vocabulary, and declarative prose without managerial signposting.

candidate_moves.reader_change: The reader experiences one argument whose concepts and formal machinery arrive in dependency order.
candidate_moves.next_possibility: The endpoint and restart can then land as the inevitable final consequence of the same-history construction.

sequence.thought: Fix the one maximal pressure-complete history and state the finite-maximality target.
sequence.connection: The proof needs quantities that can detect how this one history approaches a finite terminal time.
sequence.reader_end: The reader knows the one history and the exact contradiction target.

sequence.thought: Derive energy and the VPI law from the original equation.
sequence.connection: Energy bounds total size but still permits transfer toward high frequency, so the scale-invariant height becomes necessary.
sequence.reader_start: The reader has the one history.
sequence.reader_end: The reader has the spatial balance that distinguishes viscous loss from signed response.

sequence.thought: Use scaling and dyadic weighting to derive critical height and the finite-time escalation pressure.
sequence.connection: Unbounded motion in the critical space requires accumulated motion in the next temporal row.
sequence.reader_start: The reader sees possible high-frequency redistribution.
sequence.reader_end: The reader understands why time derivatives must enter.

sequence.thought: Derive the Eulerian temporal rows, pressure recurrence, and independent spatial derivatives from the original equation.
sequence.connection: The temporal and spatial indices now coexist on one pressure-complete history and can be compared through differentiated height.
sequence.reader_end: The reader possesses the full finite mixed jet and its one-datum origin.

sequence.thought: Differentiate critical height and retain the complete response until each temporal row exposes a spatial energy.
sequence.connection: No finite row carries all orders, so smoothness must be sought in compatibility across finite cuts.
sequence.reader_start: The reader has the mixed jet.
sequence.reader_end: The reader understands the reversible height-spatial relation and the need for an intersection.

sequence.thought: Introduce a finite rectangle as the smallest object that keeps adjacent time rows, spatial depth, pressure, and overlap identity together.
sequence.connection: The datum-generated whole-terminal theorem controls each such finite object on the complete terminal interval.
sequence.reader_start: The reader needs compatible finite cuts.
sequence.reader_end: The reader understands the rectangle's type, norm, and same-history bonding maps.

sequence.thought: Assemble the controlled rectangles through their literal overlap identities.
sequence.connection: The inverse limit returns the original velocity with every finite time and space order available.
sequence.reader_start: The reader has controlled compatible cuts.
sequence.reader_end: The reader has one all-orders mixed object, not a collection of unrelated solutions.

sequence.thought: Read height, spatial, and temporal regularity from that same object.
sequence.connection: Adjacent rows now satisfy the exact Hilbert-scale hypotheses needed for a common terminal trace.
sequence.reader_start: The reader has the projective object.
sequence.reader_end: The reader sees how the formal intersection becomes boundary regularity.

sequence.thought: Use adjacent traces to identify one common smooth endpoint for every finite rectangle.
sequence.connection: A velocity value alone restarts locally, but smooth gluing requires the actual pressure-complete endpoint jet.
sequence.reader_end: The reader has one common H-infinity endpoint and all left traces.

sequence.thought: Pass the original pressure and velocity recurrences to the endpoint.
sequence.connection: The restarted solution begins from the same value and the same complete jet.
sequence.reader_start: The reader has the endpoint traces.
sequence.reader_end: The reader has a uniquely determined pressure-complete endpoint jet.

sequence.thought: Apply the standard local theory once, glue the two histories, and contradict finite maximality.
sequence.connection: The proof ends at the concrete continuation that the maximal interval forbids.
sequence.reader_start: The reader has matching left and right jets.
sequence.reader_end: The reader sees why the same history continues and why the maximal time is infinite.
